This is a standard `.SRCINFO` file for the `noos-win-installer` AUR package, version 0.1.2, release 1. The file correctly describes the package metadata including name, description, version, dependencies, source URL, and checksum.

The source is fetched from `https://github.com/Chomiam/noos_win_installer/archive/refs/tags/v0.1.2.tar.gz`, which appears to be the legitimate upstream repository consistent with the declared `url` field. All dependencies (such as `cargo`, `git`, `gtk3`, `polkit`, etc.) are reasonable for a Rust + Tauri application that creates bootable USB drives and interacts with Windows installation media. No obfuscated code, dangerous commands, or unexpected file operations are present in this metadata file. This represents normal AUR packaging practice.

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD for noos-win-installer follows standard Arch packaging practices. It downloads the source tarball from the official GitHub repository at a specific tag, verifies it with a fixed SHA256 checksum, and builds the Rust/Tauri application using cargo with `--locked` and `--frozen` flags to ensure reproducibility. The build process is confined to the source directory, and the package function installs only expected files (binary, desktop file, icons, license, README) to standard system locations. There is no evidence of network requests to untrusted hosts, obfuscated code, dangerous commands (like eval or curl|bash), or modifications to sensitive system files. The dependencies are typical for a GUI application using GTK and webkit2gtk.
</details>
